recipes.name: Spinach Quiche with Cottage Cheese
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed
1 bunch green onions, finely chopped (white parts only)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9 inch pie or quiche pan.

Place spinach in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally until soft. Drain off any remaining liquid. Stir in green onions, eggs, cottage cheese and Cheddar cheese. Pour mixture into prepared pan.
Bake uncovered in preheated oven for 45 minutes. Remove from oven and sprinkle with crushed croutons. Return to oven and bake for an additional 15 minutes, until eggs are set.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach Quiche with Cottage Cheese
raw_recipe.description: A simple crust-less quiche with spinach, green onions and two cheeses.

review.reviewBody: This was amazing! Made a few changes though: sauteed some chopped yellow onion and a few chopped mushrooms in a bit of oil before adding 8 oz of microwaved & drained spinach. Also threw in about 1/2 c chopped sun dried tomatoes. Drained cottage cheese and mixed in with the spinach, then poured the whole thing into a greased pie plate. I sprinkled with about 1/2 c grated asiago cheese and then poured 6 beaten eggs over the top. Baked for about 50 min at 375. The sun dried tomatoes and asiago really gave the dish a lovely flavor.

This was delicious, especially considering we don't normally eat cottage cheese. I did run the cottage cheese through my mini food processor to do away with the curds, I'm amazed at the wonderful texture this imparts to the quiche, I would have never guessed. Other than that, I did increase the eggs to 6, and used fresh spinach which I sauteed with the onion. Also added garlic , onion powder, and a few sprinkles of paprika for more flavor. Next time I'll probably increase the cheese a little since I use more eggs. Thanks for the great recipe :)

Very tasty. Make sure you really squeeze all the water out of the spinach. I thought I’d been thorough but there was still a little liquid in the bottom of the dish. I used crumbled ritz crackers instead of croutons. You probably don’t need either. Definitely let it rest for 10 minutes or so before serving.

Amazing! I had some spinach and other veges I needed to use. Diced onion, bell pepper, fennel, spinach. Diced ham. I added 6 eggs because of the extra filling. I sauteed the veges first. The cottage cheese was excellent! The texture of the quiche was perfect! I added some French herb blend that I like to use. Will definitely make again!

I added:
1 small onion instead of green onions
1 red bell pepper
sautéed onion and pepper then added fresh chopped organic spinach. Cooked till all liquid was evaporated. 
Stirred in cottage cheese, cheddar cheese and then the eggs.
Instead of croutons, I used gluten-free bread crumbs mixed with some more cheddar cheese and sprinkled that on top.
It was very good. My husband had two pieces. :)

This is my go-to when we have potluck breakfast at work. Per other reviewers I add artichoke hearts, use fresh spinach and sautée onion and garlic with the spinach. And, I top with seasoned breadcrumbs instead of croutons since I always have them on hand. I always get compliments! Thanks for the recipe!

This is the basic recipe I used but changed it up a little.

I did: 1 C shredded cheddar instead of 2 and added an extra egg. I also added 1 C. of finely chopped ham and 1/4 C. finely chopped onion (instead of the green onions) & 1/4 C. Italian bread crumbs into the mixture instead of the croutons and some shakes of parmesan. Seasoned with a few shakes of garlic pwder, season salt, and s&p. Nothing on top. Baked 1 hr. in 2 qt low casserole dish. 
Lorraine E.

Similar to others, I made but altered :)

I grilled onions and mushrooms, then added the spinach
Instead of 2 cups of Cheddar, I used one Cheddar and one Swiss

I placed the crushed croutons in the bottom of the dish

Only due to time, I baked at 375 for 50 minutes and it was perfect

A new crustless favorite!! 
This recipe should be renamed to Quick Spinach Crustless Quiche ha ha!

Fabulous recipe! You really need to squeeze all the water out of the spinach, and let the quiche rest about half an hour before cutting. I also used the leaves from the spring onions and it worked really well.

This was fantastic!! I did make a couple of slight adjustments: used sautéed onions instead of raw green onions and left off the crouton topping, it didn't need it. I also used sharp cheddar (shredded). I can't believe how scrumptious this was! I'm not a big fan of spinach, but I barely tasted it in this recipe (tasted the fried onions mainly)! I used muffin tins which gives me specific portion sizes; 2 quiche muffins = lunch, along with tomato juice and an apple. The rest are in the fridge for future lunches, heat and serve. Thanks so much for this tasty carb-free option! Will definitely be making this one again!

It was delicious! I made a few changes to the recipe though...added 1 can mushroom pieces, 1 tsp all spice, 1 tsp lemon pepper, and 1 round onion. And I baked dish for 30 more minutes because middle was still wet. Took out the dish and cut it in pie pieces, middle was still a bit wet but onolicious!
This recipe is delicious ! I followed the recipe ; didn't add anything ... easy !

I used fresh spinach, as that is what I had. The recipe had nice flavour, but it was quite watery at the bottom. I think the cottage cheese should have gone through a strainer or cheese cloth as well? I might look for a different recipe next time.

I was skeptical because of the cottage cheese but this was really good. I added onion, garlic, sun dried tomatoes, basil, rosemary and oregano and subbed skim mozzarella for the cheddar. I also added paprika and chili flakes for a little kick. I’ll definitely make it again.
I used ricotta in place of cottage cheese and it came out perfect. It tastes great when reheated for lunch.
This is the only way I can get my family to eat spinach, they love this quiche! We added a can of chopped artichokes and it was so yummy!!

This recipe is the best. I have made it multiple times and it is a part of the family favorites. I did find this recipe in a cookbook about 30 years ago but lost the cookbook and could not remember the exact measures even though I had made it hundreds of times. I do remember the other recipe had flour and butter but honestly it does not need it. I make this recipe but add garlic powder and it is a big hit. No difference in taste or texture from the original one I made years ago. I admit I do not use breadcrumbs or croutons - no need. Thanks for posting this wonderful recipe.

Loved this! Wonderful crustless quiche. I made changes but the review didn't get saved somehow. Don't recall all of them, but what I do recall: 1. Next time I'll leave off the croutons. I used gf breadcrumbs and they seemed pointless. 2. I used fresh, whole spinach 3. I added fresh basil (chopped) inside 4. I put fresh basil on the top about halfway through cooking 5. I used 2 oz crumbled blue cheese rather than cheddar 6. I added red chili flake 7. Cooking time was much longer for me than indicated on recipe. My oven tends to need longer cook times, and I used a greased glass pie dish. I cooked 90-120 minutes before the middle was solid, and although the edge had pulled away from the pan by that point it was wonderfully crispy without being dry. I'll make this again!
Fabulous and so easy to make. I added turkey sausage to the mix and rather than using croutons I used crushed melba toast.
Great recipe, I added my own ingredients cause I didn’t have everything!! So yummy
